recipe.visualDefinition: A high-contrast composition featuring a black-and-white portrait of a man on a weathered street flyer with tear-off phone number tabs, pasted onto a textured utility pole, set against a dark background with bold vertical typography.
coreVisualRelationships: The flyer acts as a central frame within the larger frame of the pole.
Contrast between the organic texture of the pole and the clean, bold typography.
Vertical orientation of the main title balancing the verticality of the pole.
coreInvariants: Black and white portrait inside a hand-drawn black border
Tear-off tabs at the bottom of the flyer
90-degree rotated vertical title text on the right third

compositionAndHierarchy.subjectPositionAndScale: The flyer occupies the left two-thirds of the frame, slightly angled; the portrait is the primary focal point.
compositionAndHierarchy.visualAnchor: The large, white vertical title text on the right edge.
compositionAndHierarchy.movementAndEyePath: Eyes start at the portrait, move down to the tear-off tabs, then sweep up the vertical title on the right.
compositionAndHierarchy.negativeSpace: Dark, out-of-focus urban background provides depth and separation for the pole.

colorSystem.dominantColorRole: Off-white/Cream for the flyer and title text.
colorSystem.contrastColorRole: Deep black for the background, shadows, and flyer borders.
colorSystem.accentColorRole: Grayscale tones for the photographic portrait.
colorSystem.saturationAndValueRelationship: High value contrast with zero saturation; monochromatic palette.

typographyAndGraphicLanguage.baseSkeleton: Heavyweight slab serif and grotesque sans-serif
letterConstructionRules: Title uses ultra-bold, rounded slab serifs with tight kerning
Flyer text uses a high-contrast, bold serif with a slight hand-drawn feel
Tab text uses a condensed, functional sans-serif
characterSpecificRedesigns: Rounded terminals on the main title slab serifs
Vertical orientation for the primary title
typographyAndGraphicLanguage.pairingStrategy: Heavy decorative slab serif for branding paired with a classic editorial serif for the flyer content.

preserve: Vertical orientation of the main title

candidateDirections.reason: Matches the heavy, rounded slab-serif feel of the main title.
Provides the sturdy, classic serif look for the flyer body text.

twoStageComposition.backgroundInstruction: Generate a photo of a weathered concrete utility pole in a dark urban setting. On the pole, a paper flyer is pasted with a black and white portrait of a man inside a thick black border. The bottom of the flyer has several vertical tear-off tabs. The lighting should be dramatic and high-contrast.
twoStageComposition.overlayInstruction: Add a large, bold, white slab-serif title vertically along the right side. Add a bold serif question at the bottom of the flyer above the tabs, and small vertical phone numbers on each tab.

verificationChecks: Is the title text rotated 90 degrees vertically?
Are the tear-off tabs clearly visible at the bottom?
Is the portrait strictly black and white?
Is the background dark and out of focus?

adjustableVariables: Font weight of the vertical title
mustRedesign: Specific facial features of the actor

mustAchieve: Clear hierarchy between flyer and title

postGenerationChecks: Ensure the flyer looks physically attached to the pole.
Check that the vertical text is legible despite the rotation.
Verify the tear-off tabs have realistic spacing.
Confirm the monochrome palette is maintained.
recipe.reuseFormula: Urban Flyer Layout = [Textured Vertical Anchor] + [Weathered Paper Overlay] + [B&W Portrait] + [Vertical Display Typography]
